name: BU Seal
subtitle: Marsh Plaza · step on it and you won't graduate

source.position: Esri World Imagery (dark 3.2 m disc at the centre of the plaza's paving pattern, ~15 m in front of the chapel porch and ~2.5 m west of its axis), registered to the OSM outlines of Marsh Chapel (way/1007090937) and Marsh Plaza (way/328056586); not mapped in OSM.
source.details: BU Today, 'The Myths and Legends behind the BU Seal' (2019): BU's coat of arms in Marsh Plaza, 'black stone with bronze letters', likely installed when the chapel was finished (c. 1950), buffed before Commencement; legend says step on it before Commencement and you won't graduate (also BU Admissions, 'Terrier traditions: keep off the bronze'). Restored in the 1999 plaza rebuilding (BU Bridge, 27 Aug 1999). Design from BU Today's photos: verdigris bronze rings, scrolls lettered BOSTON UNIVERSITY and LEARNING · VIRTUE · PIETY, the shield with the floriated cross and three crowns in polished bronze.
source.unverified: Exact diameter (3.1-3.2 m measured from imagery) and the orientation (modelled reading upright from Commonwealth Ave, its top toward the chapel, as in the photos).

source.details: BU Alumni / BU Today: 'between the BU Beach and the Alan & Sherry Leventhal Admissions Center', unveiled Aug 2019, donated by the BU Alumni Council; pose from The Daily Free Press photo (Aug 2019), which shows the Charles behind the bench.

source.details: OSM tags direction=245;65 (double-sided), lit=yes; 60 ft square (Wikipedia, 'Citgo sign'); on the roof of 660 Beacon St, whose model top is 23.0 m in building-models.json; logo geometry from Wikimedia Commons File:Citgo_logo.svg; truss, pyramid trimark, 39 white light rows and 18 lit triangles from the Boston Landmarks Commission Citgo Sign study report (2018); frame and catwalk also from Commons photos (2017, 2025).
source.unverified: Height of the truss: the Landmarks report says the sign is held 40 ft above the roof by a 90 ft truss (inconsistent); modelled at 9.5 m (31 ft), as photos suggest. The sign was taken down in May 2026 to be reinstalled about 120 ft east and 30 ft higher on the same property (Boston Globe, 29 May 2026; a Sept 2026 Commons photo shows the new frame). This entry is the long-standing position.
